A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Puppet-CNN work. All pages, including figures, tables, equations and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original classification experiments, ablations and model-size analyses on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and mini-ImageNet.

after.justification: Section 4 retains those original empirical results and adds a partial-versus-full CIFAR-10 training-set comparison in Table 4.

M1.justification: Kernel resizing is specified as 2D average pooling in v1 Section 3.5 and 3D average pooling in v2 Section 4.2, a limited reported procedural revision. The ODE/Euler generator, entropy combination, depth rule and initialization remain equivalent. The broader continuous-dynamics framing does not establish a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and mini-ImageNet. The added full-training-set CIFAR-10 experiment changes data quantity within existing coverage, without introducing another dataset, task or population.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DFN, WeightNet, DDFN-SW, BranchyNet, SkipNet and DRNN; the lightweight and backbone comparisons also retain their methods. The new full-data comparison extends the existing AlexNet, VGG and ResNet versus Puppet pairings.

E3.justification: V2 Table 4 adds a complete-training-set CIFAR-10 regime alongside the retained 10,000-sample subset regime. The principal settings remain 800 epochs, Adam, batch size 64 and a 512-channel maximum. The new table does not fully specify validation handling for its full-set regime.

E4.justification: V2 Table 4 adds a training-data-scale analysis testing whether the Puppet-Puppeteer scheme remains effective beyond limited-data training. Existing parameter/depth ablations and depth/channel-size analyses are retained; separating the latter into Section 4.6 does not constitute another new analysis.

E5.justification: V2 Section 4.1 newly states that the mini-ImageNet split uses a fixed random seed, without giving its value. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or experimental variability. This is additional seed disclosure, not evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: Matched existing tables and Figure 4 retain their numerical results. V2 Table 4 adds full-set Top-1/Top-5 results: for example, fixed AlexNet versus its Puppet variant achieves 80.89% versus 83.75% Top-1, while ResNet achieves 82.24% versus 80.47%. These are newly reported settings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: V1 Section 3.1's residual-network-to-feature-space-ODE derivation and shared-kernel formulation are removed. The proposed method's parameter ODE, Euler update and entropy-based adaptation equations are otherwise mathematically retained under revised notation. Neither version provides a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contributions on compression, input adaptation and broad superiority in performance and efficiency. V2 redefines the central contribution around continuous parameter dynamics and depth interpreted through integration, while narrowing the empirical claim to competitive classification performance with fewer stored parameters.

C2.justification: V2 removes the brain-emulation rationale and asserted superiority over RNN-based adaptation, acknowledges alternative sequential parameterizations, and describes entropy as a replaceable complexity proxy. It also interprets the new full-data results and explains quadratic channel-size scaling. The principal compression and computational-overhead interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 removes the explicit specification of the central trainable puppeteer as a one-layer depthwise-separable convolution with batch normalization and tanh, and omits v1's stated cross-entropy objective. It adds PyTorch, learning-rate endpoints of 1e-3 and 1e-5, and a promise of code release upon acceptance. Losing the generator specification materially affects reproducibility.

R1.justification: The model-compression related-work section is replaced by a taxonomy contrasting layer-wise generation and global parameter synthesis with continuous parameter evolution. Compression, quantization and distillation references are removed, along with the Neural Ordinary Differential Equations reference. Previously cited diffusion-based weight-generation papers receive expanded positioning rather than constituting new citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, methodology and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Methodology is reorganized around continuous evolution and trajectory sampling; implementation details move into the experiments section, and depth/channel analyses receive a separate section. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The architecture illustrations are substantially revised: Figure 1 becomes a parameter-trajectory overview, the adaptive architecture is redrawn, and a tensor-reshaping diagram replaces the earlier Euler-cell illustration. V2 adds Table 4, changes the computational-cost table's columns, transposes the channel-size table and places the two datasets side by side in Table 6. Figure 4 retains its plotted evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves claim calibration and presentation, and Table 4 adds useful evidence about training-data scale. However, it removes the central puppeteer's architecture and stated loss, weakening reproducibility despite adding optimization details; it also drops the foundational Neural ODE citation. These material benefits and harms leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
